description.narrative: Enhancing peace and stability in Krenik & Habila localities of West Darfur State. The project beneficiaries include IDPs, returnees and host communities.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
UNDP as the Implementing Partner will comply with the policies, procedures and practices of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS.)

description.narrative: - Livelihood and natural resource management (NRM) activities to reduce the competition over natural resources implemented. - Access of women and youth to income sources through enrollment in income generating activities (IGAs) increased.

comment.narrative:
Output 2: Ensure peace dividends for community interdependence and co-existence are delivered through diverse livelihoods options and effective natural resource management:
- 30 Groups - 750 members (400 women, 350 men): 28 of the groups are active and have total savings of 7,032,000 SDGs with a social fund totaling 211,800 SDGs.

2021-2022 Targets:
Output 1: Community-based conflict resolution and reconciliation mechanisms (CBRMs) are in use and working effectively to resolve conflict: - Establishing & strengthening inclusive CBRMs - Train community leaders, CBRMs, on conflict prevention and resolutions. - Organize and strengthen youth committees to play active role in conflict identification, analysis, mapping, and involvement in the decision making process. - Promote public awareness that help communities build trust on CBRMs contributions to peacebuilding and community cohesion. - Support the CBRMs conduct inclusive community/youth dialogue at the intra/inter community level. - Establishment and strengthening of inclusive crop protection committees. - conduct training to key stakeholders to build their capacity in peacebuilding, conflict resolution, reconciliation, and conflict-sensitive programming. - Empower local stakeholders and the CBRMs to develop conflict sensitive early warning and information systems for early detection of conflicts. - Train CBRMs on conflict tracking systems, recording and reporting conflicts.
Output 2: Peace dividends for community interdependence and coexistence are delivered: - Establish and strengthen the of CBRMs at the admin unit/village, locality, and state level. - Train women and youth members on employability and entrepreneurship skills. - Train/support the youth and women’s groups in to engage in honey production, value chain development (VCD), oil crop processing and marketing, hand crafting vocational skills, small scale trading, etc. - Construct/rehabilitate water supply infrastructure (hand pumps, hand dug wells. - Train CBRMs,communities, local leaders and stakeholders on gender mainstreaming. - Establish natural resource management (NRM) committees. - Support community based structures to that contribute to child protection risks.
Output 3: Women´s organizations, including those representing pastoralist women, will be empowered to meaningfully participate in local and state-level peacebuilding platforms: - Establish/strengthen women’s committees and building their capacity. - Establishment and strengthening of the women committees’ network. - Conduct large scale awareness campaigns on the negative impact of harmful gender practices like sexual violence, killings, recruitment of boys as child soldiers. - Conduct preliminary research and knowledge development to improve knowledge, understanding of women on various practices.
Output 4: Improved networking, coordination, and learning between local and state-level peacebuilding institutions: - Establishing/strengthening networks of the CBRMs, government & other CBOs, police, judiciary bodies at the locality and state level. - Supporting the link between the community level conflict resolution mechanisms and the formal judiciary mechanisms at state level. - Collaborating with the neighboring states (Central & North Darfur states) and neighboring localities to minimize regional and cross-border conflict connected livestock migration and armed conflicts. - conducting coherence, learning, and experience sharing from other universities and research centers to improve peacebuilding programming and trust between the stakeholders. - strengthening “vertical” coordination with State-level peacebuilding mechanisms, as well as with key Government entities at the local and State level, such as the Ministry of Social Affairs / Welfare, the Peace and Development Centers, HAC, etc. - Training security service providers (police, judiciary bodies) on human rights, gender and child protection, setting up locality level participatory security committees, combatting GBV, and investing in formal and informal justice.
